_comment: Canned replies for --dry-run. A list is played in order, one item per earlier turn by the same speaker.

key_hypotheses: The job hypothesis describes a real, recent struggle, not a general wish
The current workaround costs time, accuracy or independence
The current workaround is good enough and nothing would change
prep.interviewee_profile: Someone in this segment who has done a leveling task in the last month. Screen out anyone who has never done one.
starter_questions: Tell me about the last time you had to get something level.
What made that the day you did it?
Who else was around while you worked?
How did you know it was straight?
When did you find out whether it really was level?
contrasting_questions: Was the bigger problem the time it took or the result?
Why that method rather than asking someone for help?
What's worse about your current method than the one before it?
Would you rather it be faster or more accurate?

interviewer.question: Tell me about the last time you had to get something level.
How did you know it was straight?
What did you do when it turned out to be off?

user: It was a set of shelves a couple of weeks ago. I'd put it off for a while, then finally did it on a Saturday morning.
I used the level app on my phone and checked it twice. Honestly I wasn't completely sure until someone else looked at it.
I took the bracket down, moved it a bit and redid one screw. It added maybe half an hour, which was annoying but not the end of the world.
